newsitem.title: USA: Texaco forms independent equality task force.
newsitem.headline: Texaco forms independent equality task force.

text.p: Texaco Inc., fulfilling terms of last year's settlement of a race discrimination case, said Monday it formed an independent task force to monitor improvements in its human resources programmes.

The task force will be headed by Deval Patrick, a former U.S. assistant attorney general who headed the Justice Department's civil rights division between 1994 and 1996. Patrick is curently a partner at the Boston, Mass., law firm of Day, Berry & Howard.

The task force was formed as part of a settlement Texaco reached in November of a racial discrimination lawsuit filed against it by six black employees in 1994, the company said. Plaintiffs valued the settlement at $176 million.
The seven members of the panel were selected by Texaco, the nation's third largest oil company, and plaintiffs counsel, it said.
- John Gibbons, a retired chief judge of the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit and currently professor at Seton Hall University Law School, Newark, N.J.
- Jeffalyn Johnson, president and chief executive officer, Integrated Quality Solutions Inc., Alexandria, Va.
- Allen Krowe, Texaco vice chairman, who is retiring from the company on June 30
- Mari Matsuda, professor, Georgetown University Law Centre, Washington, D.C.
- Luis Nogales, president, Nogales Partners, Los Angeles
- Thomas Williamson, partner at Covington & Burling, Washington, D.C., law firm.
Texaco, based in White Plains, N.Y., settled the suit after tape recordings showed executives allegedly plotting to destroy documents and making racist remarks.
